correctness.rationale: Gesmundo--Meroni Example 8.1 supplies the exact quartic. Rewriting it with \(p=x_2+i x_3\) and \(q=x_2-i x_3\) factors all four derivatives and yields an exhaustive singular-point case split. The origin normal form \(PQ-u^2v^2\) has Jacobian ideal \((P,Q,uv^2,u^2v)\), radical \((P,Q,uv)\), and a one-dimensional square-zero nilradical quotient generated by \(uv\); the four vertex normal forms \(U^2+Vpq\) have radical singular ideals. Explicit Hessian minors establish transverse \(A_1\) type elsewhere. The embedded exact script reproduces the critical identities and local-algebra checks. Risk: the claim is affine and characteristic-zero only.
